final_answer: The bug was in `parse_amount` in `ledger/money.py`: the fraction was read as an integer without padding, so `.5` became 5 cents instead of 50. It now pads the fraction to two digits, and I added regression assertions for `10.5`, `10`, and `-0.5` to `tests/test_ledger.py`. All 3 tests pass with `python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -t .`.
I added `Journal.entries_for`, `reports.register`, and `reports.format_register`, and a new test covers them along with the unknown-account errors. The full suite passes (4 tests, OK).

The bare `ValueError` is gone from `ledger/`, and all five tests pass (`Ran 5 tests … OK`). The new `ledger/errors.py` holds `LedgerError`, the five subclasses that also inherit `ValueError`, and `ImportRowError`, which `import_csv` raises with the 1-based line from the CSV reader. I also updated the `parse_amount` docstring to name `InvalidAmount` and added tests for the error types and the import row error.

The bug was in `percentile` in `logkit/stats.py`, which picked index `int(p/100 * n)` rather than the nearest-rank index `ceil(p/100 * n) - 1`. I changed it to compute the rank with `math.ceil(p * n / 100)`, keeping the same signature, and added regression cases for the reported inputs (p50 of 1..4 gives 2, p95 of 1..20 gives 19). The test suite passes (3 tests, OK).

All three features are in: `--since`/`--until` (UTC timestamps only, with `--since` inclusive and `--until` exclusive), `--json` output, and `render.json_line`. The suite passes (11 tests), including new tests for the boundaries, bad timestamps, JSON key order, and `--summary` taking precedence over `--json`.

One choice beyond the spec: `--since`/`--until` reject naive timestamps like `2026-01-05T10:00:00`, because without a zone they would be read as local time. Both `Z` and `+00:00` are accepted.

Records are now `Record` dataclasses in `logkit/record.py`, and every module and the CLI use attribute access. The unit tests pass (4/4), and no dict-style record access remains in `logkit/`. CLI output matched the original across seven argument sets; the one difference was only the temp-directory paths in an identical traceback for an invalid `--level`.

Tax was being computed on the pre-discount subtotal in `shop/pricing.py`'s `total()`, so every coupon left tax overcharged. It now applies to the subtotal minus the discount, and I added a regression test for a $40 SAVE10 cart in CA (tax $2.61, total $38.61). All 5 tests pass, and no public names or signatures changed.

final_answer: Money in `shop/` is now integer cents throughout: `Item.price_cents`, `tax.RATES_BP` with the half-up integer tax and discount formulas, `fmt.money` on cents, and the CLI reading `price_cents`. The test suite passes (8 tests), and a grep finds no `float`, `round(`, or decimal literals left in `shop/`. I updated the existing tests to cents and added cases for the half-up rounding, the FIVEOFF threshold, and unknown coupons and regions.

The bug was in `should_retry` in `taskq/retry.py`: it used `job.attempts <= job.max_attempts`, which allowed one extra run because `attempts` is incremented when the job is popped. I changed it to `<`, so a job now runs exactly `max_attempts` times. I also added a regression test in `tests/test_taskq.py` that counts handler calls for a job that always fails, and all 4 tests pass.

Job dependencies are in: `enqueue` takes `depends_on` and rejects unknown ids, `pop_ready` waits for dependencies to be done, and a `fail` that kills a job cascades `"dead"` with `"dependency failed: <root id>"` to queued dependents. `depends_on` round-trips through `dump`/`load`, and old dumps load with an empty list. The suite passes (10 tests, including new ones for each rule).

One behavior you didn't specify: enqueuing a job whose dependency is already dead creates it as dead immediately, with the same error, so it can't sit queued forever.

The job status is now a `Status` enum in `taskq/jobs.py`, and `queue.py` and `store.py` use its members. The string literals now appear only in `jobs.py`, and `store.py` writes and reads the plain string. All 6 tests pass, including new ones for the default status, the plain-string dump, and loading an old dump file.

The bold regex in `wiki/inline.py` was greedy (`.+`), so it spanned from the first `**` to the last. I made it lazy (`.+?`) and added a regression test, `test_two_bold_phrases`, in `tests/test_wiki.py`. All 4 tests pass.

All three features are in: ordered lists (`olist` blocks), a `[TOC]` block that lists every heading in the document, and unique heading slugs (`-2`, `-3`, ...) shared by the `<hN>` ids, the TOC links, and `toc.build`. I added tests for each, and all 7 pass with `python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -t .`.

The tuples are now dataclasses (`Heading`, `Para`, `ListBlock`, `Code`) in `wiki/blocks.py`, and `html.render` and `toc.build` dispatch on them with `isinstance`, raising `ValueError("unknown block: ...")` for anything else. The five tests pass, including new ones for the dataclass output and the unknown-block error, and a grep finds none of the forbidden quoted strings left in `wiki/`.
